risk_ledger.trigger_condition: local feedback reset is mistaken for real download or support integration
risk_ledger.pm_decision: keep all auxiliary feedback behavior prototype_only and not_integrated
risk_ledger.mitigation_or_owner: design, test-design, developer, QA, and delivery-owner preserve boundary markers

risk_ledger.trigger_condition: phase-2 dogfood mutates phase-1 signoff or creates user-decision.json without explicit user decision

risk_ledger.mitigation_or_owner: delivery-owner verifies phase-1 remains untouched for user decision state

review_conclusion.summary: phase-2 PM scope is ready for design and task planning

business_flows: User clicks download/support entries, sees local feedback counts, clears them, and verifies refresh-safe defaults.
user_paths: Download feedback increment and reset path.
Support feedback increment and reset path.
rule_mappings: RULE-1: phase-2 may only change local static prototype feedback behavior.
RULE-2: no phase-2 artifact may create phase-1 user-decision.json or claim real integration.

options: dedicated clear buttons near each auxiliary status
single shared reset control for both auxiliary statuses
design_decision_candidates.constraints: must remain local to the static prototype and be easy to verify in desktop and mobile browsers
design_decision_candidates.design_handoff: choose reset control placement and local state behavior without adding persistence or backend calls

coverage_matrix.action_or_path: click download entry twice and clear download feedback
click support entry twice and clear support feedback

technical_evidence_requirements.business_invariant: Feedback reset must be local-only and must not call backend, external navigation, download, support, telemetry, auth, release, or rollback paths.
technical_evidence_requirements.required_downstream_proof: Developer and QA must use real browser evidence and network inspection or implementation review to prove no external integration was introduced.

unsupported_platforms: download, support, telemetry, auth, release, and rollback paths
